chapter_seo_title: A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality Ch. 296 — Han Li's Psychological Domination
chapter_meta_description: Han Li forces a grandfather-granddaughter duo into a trade through pure psychological pressure. In the Mortal Stream, the best weapons are often invisible.
og_title: RMJI Ch. 296: The Art of the Unfair Trade
og_description: Han Li demonstrates that in the Mortal Stream, a negotiation is won before the first word is spoken.
twitter_description: Han Li wins a deal by breaking a girl's courage before he says a single word of trade.

lore_anchors.definition: A low-grade spell that plants a strand of the caster's spiritual sense into a target, allowing them to be tracked over long distances. In the Mortal Stream, it serves as a psychological leash.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Han Li plant a tracking mark instead of just trusting them?
cultural_notes_faq.a: In the Mortal Stream, trust is a vulnerability. The tracking mark is a low-cost insurance policy that guarantees the deal will happen regardless of the other party's intentions.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Does the old man have any chance to escape?
cultural_notes_faq.a: No. Once Han Li deployed the tracking mark, the only choice left is whether to comply gracefully or to flee and be hunted. The old man is a seasoned enough survivor to choose wisely.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is the girl fascinated by Han Li's exit technique?
cultural_notes_faq.a: She has likely never seen a Foundation Establishment cultivator act with such casual, absolute control. In the Mortal Stream, power is the ultimate aphrodisiac, and even a fourteen-year-old recognizes it.
